challenges.name: rebuild-leaderboard-quiz
challenges.title: What do readers see during a rebuild?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from rebuilding the all-time board: a replay script that works on the live key, and a swap followed by a catch-up from the watermark.

questions.question:
The first rebuild script (pseudo-code) and what the leaderboard API returned while it ran:

DEL lb:all
for each page of 1,000 rows of score_events ORDER BY id:
    MULTI
    ZINCRBY lb:all <points> <learnerId>     -- one per row
    EXEC

10:00:02  GET /leaderboard?board=all  -> top 3: u_0815 40, u_1001 30, u_2040 20
10:00:19  GET /leaderboard?board=all  -> top 3: u_0815 2210, u_1001 1650, u_2040 1490
10:00:41  GET /leaderboard?board=all  -> top 3: u_0815 4380, u_2040 3720, u_1001 3600   (script finished)

Statement: "Because each page runs inside MULTI/EXEC, readers can only see the board before the rebuild or the finished board."
questions.explanation: False. MULTI/EXEC makes each page atomic: no reader sees half of a page. It does nothing for the time between pages, and DEL lb:all already ran before the first page, so every read during those 40 seconds saw a board that was empty or partly rebuilt - exactly the low scores in the log. To hide the whole rebuild, build into another key (lb:all:rebuild) and swap it in with RENAME, which replaces lb:all in one step. The misconception is that atomic pieces make the whole sequence atomic.

questions.question:
The fixed rebuild, with the live consumer running all the time (it marks each event id in lb:seen and skips ids it finds there):

10:20:00.000  watermark = SELECT max(id) FROM score_events  -> 1840
10:20:00.010  build lb:all:rebuild + lb:seen:rebuild from ids 1..1840
10:20:05.300  live consumer: event 1841 -> applied to lb:all (old board)
10:20:09.870  MULTI; RENAME lb:all:rebuild lb:all; RENAME lb:seen:rebuild lb:seen; EXEC
10:20:09.902  live consumer: event 1842 -> applied to lb:all (new board), marked in lb:seen
10:20:09.950  catch-up: replay ids > 1840 through the same dedupe -> 1841 applied, 1842 skipped (already in lb:seen)

Statement: "After the catch-up the board contains event 1841 and event 1842 exactly once each, even though 1842 was both delivered live and read by the catch-up."
questions.explanation: True. Event 1841 went to the old board, which the RENAME threw away, and it is not in the new lb:seen (built from ids up to 1840), so the catch-up applies it to the new board. Event 1842 was applied to the new board after the swap and marked in the new lb:seen, so the catch-up finds it and skips it. Replaying from the watermark is safe precisely because the replay goes through the same dedupe as the live path. The misconception is that a catch-up must know which events the live consumer already handled; the dedupe on the event id answers that for it.

challenges.name: rebuild-leaderboard-from-log
challenges.title: Rebuild the leaderboard while events keep arriving
challenges.description:
CodeDev's all-time leaderboard in Redis has drifted from PostgreSQL (a consumer bug applied some events twice), so it must be rebuilt from the event log - without taking the leaderboard down and without losing the events learners earn while the rebuild runs. PostgreSQL score_events (id bigserial, learner_id, points) is the source of truth: one row per graded pass, and a correction row with negative points when a pass is revoked. A live consumer keeps applying new rows to Redis during the rebuild; it delivers at least once, so the same event can arrive again. The starter has the in-memory Redis model (hset, zincrby, del, exists, rename - a missing source is an error, as in Redis - and more) and FakeDb with maxEventId() and eventsAfter(afterId, limit) (rows with id > afterId ordered by id, 1 <= limit <= 100).

Keys: lb:all (sorted set, member = learnerId, score = the sum of the points of the events applied to it) and lb:seen (hash, field = event id as a decimal string, value "1": the events lb:all contains); during a rebuild the same pair is built as lb:all:rebuild and lb:seen:rebuild.

Write applyEvent(redis, boardKey, seenKey, event) - the live consumer calls it as applyEvent(redis, "lb:all", "lb:seen", event) - returning "invalid" when id is not a positive safe integer, learnerId not a non-empty string or points not a safe integer (negative and 0 are allowed), with nothing changed and the id not marked; "duplicate" when the id is already a field of seenKey; otherwise "applied": mark the id in seenKey and ZINCRBY boardKey by points.

Write rebuild(redis, db): (1) delete lb:all:rebuild and lb:seen:rebuild, which a crashed rebuild may have left behind; (2) watermark = db.maxEventId(), then read the events with id <= watermark in pages of at most 100 and apply them to the :rebuild keys; (3) swap: RENAME lb:all:rebuild to lb:all, then lb:seen:rebuild to lb:seen, back to back (in production both run in one MULTI/EXEC); if the log had no events, DEL lb:all and lb:seen instead; (4) catch-up: replay every event with id > watermark, page by page until a page comes back empty, through applyEvent on lb:all and lb:seen. Events the live consumer wrote to the old board were lost by the swap and must be applied again; events it already wrote to the new board are duplicates. Readers of lb:all must never see a half-built board, and the final board must equal every event in the log applied exactly once.

The runner delivers live events while rebuild runs: before every DB query and right before the swap (your first RENAME). Input (stdin): { "log": [[id, learnerId, points]], "board"?, "seen"?, "leftover"?, "live"?: [[event]], "summary"?: true }. Output: the final board, whether it matches every event applied once, the number of seen ids and of log rows, the lb:* keys left, and whether a reader ever saw a half-built board. Do not change the types, FakeClock, FakeRedis, FakeDb or the test runner.
hints: Split the events into two groups by one number you read before anything else. Which group can you build quietly where nobody looks, and which group has to be replayed after the swap - and what makes replaying an event that may already be on the board harmless?

Look at the return value of hset (1 for a new field, 0 for an existing one), at what you do when the log was empty (there is nothing to RENAME), at the keys a crashed rebuild may have left, and at the moment the live consumer writes to lb:all: before the swap its writes land on a board that is about to be replaced.

The same shape on a different index, a search index of course titles: read max(id) = 500 from course_revisions; build search:courses:next from revisions 1..500 in pages; RENAME it over search:courses; then read revisions with id > 500 until a page is empty and apply each one only if its id is not yet in search:courses:applied. A revision 503 indexed live after the swap is skipped by the replay; revision 501, indexed live into the old key before the swap, is applied again.
